answer: Continuous physical-presence attestation. Each identity must periodically prove occupancy of a distinct fixed site whose sensors record unique environmental noise—say, the vibration signature of a basalt outcrop—so one operator cannot reproduce many sites at once. A registered garden terrace anchors each node's readings to its own microclimate and soil chemistry. Faking N identities then costs N separate physical installations plus N leases, since a single room yields one signature.
